newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-MEXICO OVERCOME PENALTY PHOBIA TO REACH SEMIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICO OVERCOME PENALTY PHOBIA TO REACH SEMIS.

text.p: Mexico overcame their penalty shoot-out phobia as they beat Ecuador to reach the Copa America semifinals Sunday.

Mexico's last two World Cup campaigns have ended with heavy penalty shoot-out defeats, against Germany in 1986 and Bulgaria in 1994, but on Sunday they won 4-3 on penalties after the teams had played to a 1-1 draw.
Their marksmanship still left much to be desired as they missed two of their attempts but they were helped by goalkeeper Adolfo Rios, who saved three Ecuadorean efforts.
Mexico travel to high-altitude La Paz to face host nation Bolivia in Wednesday's first semifinal.

Ecuador, who held Argentina and surprisingly beat Paraguay on their way to winning their first round group, made an early breakthrough when captain Luis Capurro, who missed his attempt in the shoot-out, scored from the penalty spot.
In what seemed a harsh decision on Mexico, the penalty was awarded after Ecuador's Ariel Graziani went tumbling over as he tussled for the ball with Duilio Davino.
Cuauhtemoc Blanco equalised 12 minutes later and the Mexicans missed three excellent chances as they dominated the rest of the first half.
The second half was more even with Ecuador, knocked out by Mexico in the semifinals four years ago, creating the better chances.
Ecuador and Mexico both left their top players behind as they are concentrating their efforts on qualifying for the World Cup next year.
Ecuador's Colombian coach Francisco Maturana delegated command of the team to his assistant Luis Fernando Suarez.

Ecuador: 12-Geovanny Ibarra, 2-Marcos Constante, 3-Ulises de la Cruz, 4-Edmundo Mendez, 5-Maximo Tenorio (14-Alberto Montano, 46), 6-Luis Capurro, 8-Hector Carabali, 7-Wellington Sanchez (15-Vilson Rosero, 82), 10-Jose Gavica (11-Angel Fernandez, 75), 20-Ariel Graziani, 9-Eduardo Hurtado.

Mexico: 1-Adolfo Rios, 13-Pavel Pardo (10-Eustacio Rizo, 55), 2-Claudio Suarez, 5-Duilio Davino, 4-German Villa, 6-Rafael Lara, 3-Joel Sanchez, 14-Camilo Romero, 8-Nicolas Ramirez (9- Paulo Cesar Chaver, 62), 11-Cuauhetemoc Blanco, 15-Luis Hernandez.
